hints.title: Algebraic Complex Expansion Formula
hints.text: Multiplying two complex numbers (a + bi) and (c + di) yields (ac - bd) for real part and (ad + bc) for imaginary part since i^2 = -1.

hints.title: String Component Delimiter Parsing
hints.text: Parse strings by finding the plus sign and trailing i character to cleanly separate real and imaginary parts as signed integers.

hints.title: Formatted Output String Assembly
hints.text: Compute real = a * c - b * d and imag = a * d + b * c. Format and return the result string as real + "+" + imag + "i".

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def complexNumberMultiply(self, num1: str, num2: str) -> str:
        a, b = map(int, num1[:-1].split("+"))
        c, d = map(int, num2[:-1].split("+"))
        real = a * c - b * d
        imag = a * d + b * c
        return f"{real}+{imag}i"
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Manual character parsing without standard delimiters increases off-by-one errors with negative coefficients.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Splitting on plus sign parses components in constant time and computes closed form in O(1) operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle negative values in real and imaginary parts without failing regex or splits.

class Solution:
    def complexNumberMultiply(self, num1: str, num2: str) -> str:
        a, b = map(int, num1[:-1].split("+"))
        c, d = map(int, num2[:-1].split("+"))
        real = a * c - b * d
        imag = a * d + b * c
        return f"{real}+{imag}i"
